source_batch.unit_label: BRBL::MOD_C::U14: Compute the stated RDB appeal deposit without importing the SARFAESI debt base

payload.title: Use the determined debt for this RDB exercise
payload.core_explanation_md: Assume an eligible section21 RDB appeal and Tribunal-determined debt INR840,000. No reduction order exists. Calculate the ordinary 50% deposit; do not import the lower-of-two-amounts rule from a different statute.

self_check.prompt_text: Which rule and stipulated facts determine this result?
self_check.expected_takeaway: Use the sourced rule and stated scenario assumptions; the arithmetic does not establish a live legal entitlement.

payload.stem_md: For an otherwise eligible RDB section21 appeal, assume Tribunal-determined debt INR1,180,000 and no reduction order. Calculate the ordinary50% deposit in exact INR.
payload.correct_explanation_md: 1180000*50/100=590000 INR. The stated base is Tribunal-determined debt.

numeric_rule.rounding_instruction: Use exact whole units; do not round intermediate values.

payload.stem_md: A learning note reads the source word waive as allowing an automatic zero deposit despite the expressed25% minimum. Which correction is needed?

options.text_md: Preserve the statutory floor and distinguish requested from granted reduction
options.explanation_md: The minimum cannot be erased by an isolated word.

options.text_md: Always choose zero when the borrower asks
options.explanation_md: A request does not establish lawful relief.

options.text_md: Use collateral value instead of the specified debt base
options.explanation_md: The deposit base is defined by the provision.

options.text_md: Replace the appeal fee with a deposit and omit one entirely
options.explanation_md: Fee and deposit are different requirements.

payload.correct_explanation_md: The minimum cannot be erased by an isolated word.
